headline: No plausible pairwise risk: both open-source docs-only profiles are non-runnable, network-egress is none, and no shared I/O surfaces are documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented between awesome-python and spring-integration-samples. Both profiles show empty io_surfaces and network_egress:none, so there is no plausible default path for one agent’s outputs to be ingested as instructions by the other.
conditions: IF a shared clipboard, filesystem, or MCP bridge is added later, injection risk becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep the pair isolated with no shared workspace.
Do not add clipboard-based handoff between the agents.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a shared channel is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Neither profile touches data classes, and both have network_egress:none. With no documented shared workspace or authenticated principal, there is no credible default leakage path from awesome-python to spring-integration-samples or vice versa.
conditions: IF either agent is later granted access to sensitive files or outbound network, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of any shared directory.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: The profiles expose no write capabilities, no concurrency model, and no shared mutable resource. Because awesome-python and spring-integration-samples are both non-runnable docs-only artifacts, a write-write conflict is not plausible from the documented pair.
conditions: IF either profile gains filesystem, git, or database write access to the same target, conflict risk appears.
mitigations: Avoid mounting a shared writable directory.
Do not grant git write access to either agent.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared mutable state is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: There is no documented pipeline where awesome-python’s output becomes spring-integration-samples’ authoritative input, and both are non-runnable docs-only profiles. Without an action-taking downstream agent or verified handoff, cascading error is not supported by the evidence.
conditions: IF one agent is later configured to consume the other’s output as authoritative, cascading error becomes possible.
mitigations: Insert a human verification step before any handoff.
Do not auto-execute actions from either agent’s output.
requires-engineering: add validation gates for downstream consumers.

E_compliance.rationale: No data residency, certification, retention, or regulated data classes are documented for either awesome-python or spring-integration-samples. Because the profiles are docs-only and touch no data classes, there is no evidenced compliance mismatch to assess.
conditions: IF regulated data is later routed through either agent, compliance review is required.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Document residency and retention before deployment.
requires-engineering: add policy controls if regulated data is introduced.
